citation: Gilad I, Nissan M. Sagittal evaluation of elemental geometrical dimensions of human vertebrae. J. Anat. (1985), 143, 115-120 (no issue number printed). Copy read: greg's upload of 2026-10-28 17:00 UTC, project files literature/synthetic_spine/gilad1985.pdf, sha256 begins f15c058eaf36fa62.
population: Living healthy working men, 20-38 years (mean 26.8), mean stature 174.7 cm, employees of a major transportation cooperative with periodic check-ups; country and ethnicity not stated (Inference: Israel, authors at the Technion, Haifa). Radiographs of 141 cervical spines and 157 lumbar spines (p. 115, PDF 1); summary says 157 men (p. 120, PDF 6); overlap not stated. Measurements per level: C2 130, C3 141, C4 141, C5 141, C6 140, C7 126; L1 154, L2 157, L3 157, L4 157, L5 156 (Tables 1-2, p. 118, PDF 4); Inference: 819 cervical and 781 lumbar vertebra-measurements. Subjects with bone degeneration or any known disease or abnormality excluded; only clearly defined vertebrae examined (p. 115, PDF 1).
modality: Plain lateral radiographs, one cervical plate (standing, neutral, tube-film 150 cm, centred on C4) and one lumbar plate (lying on the side, knees flexed, tube-film 100 cm, centred on L3), same apparatus and film for all; five reference points marked per vertebra, distances by calipers (and compass) on film to 0.1 mm, alpha and L computed by trigonometry, all corrected for parallax to the mid-sagittal plane (object-to-film distance not given). pp. 115-117, 119 (PDF 1, 3, 5).
levels_covered: C2-C7 and L1-L5. C1 hidden by the skull in every film; thoracic spine not evaluated because of rib overlap; sacrum not measured (p. 117, PDF 3).

anomalies.variant: Transitional and numerical anomalies (LSTV, sacralisation, lumbarisation, L6, T13, rib counts, cervical ribs, block vertebrae)
anomalies.finding: Not mentioned; no prevalence given. Numbering assumes seven cervical and five lumbar vertebrae (C2-C7 plate, L1-L5 plate). Inference: the exclusion of any known abnormality and the selection of clearly defined vertebrae filtered such anatomy out of the sample.
anomalies.how_identified: Not described; each vertebra 'clearly identified and marked' by region and number on the lateral film

anomalies.finding: L1 n 154 (3 missing of 157), L5 n 156 (1 missing), C6 n 140 (1 missing of 141), none explained; C2 n 130 and C7 n 126 explained as about 10 percent unclear (C2) or obscured by clavicle, humerus and ribs (C7).

measures.name: Five reference points P1-P5
measures.definition: P1 most supero-anterior body point (b meets c); P2 most supero-posterior (c meets d); P3 most infero-anterior (a meets b); P4 most infero-posterior (a meets d); P5 most posterior point of the spinous process, 'on the line parallel to b' (tangent parallel to the anterior wall, read with Fig. 1). 'Width' means antero-posterior depth on the lateral film; 'length' is the antero-posterior length of the whole vertebra.
measures.ct_mask_recipe: Inference: per-instance frame (left-right normal to the symmetry plane, AP along inferior end plate, cranio-caudal normal to both); project the mask along left-right to a lateral silhouette (closest to the film) and also cut the mid-sagittal slice; take corners and spinous tip from the silhouette.
measures.radiograph_recipe: Lateral film; mark P1-P5 before measuring; correct for magnification to the mid-sagittal plane.
measures.error: Calipers < +/-0.5 mm; parallax correction up to +/-1.0 mm more

measures.name: a, inferior width of body (lower end-plate depth)
measures.ct_mask_recipe: AP extent of the body subregion along the inferior end plate between antero-inferior and postero-inferior corners (Inference: rim corners, osteophytes excluded).
measures.radiograph_recipe: Lateral only, corner to corner, divided by magnification; not on AP.
measures.level_pattern: Rises slowly C2 to C6 (peak 16.6), C7 slightly lower; lumbar flat 33.9-34.9, smallest L5; no significant lumbar differences (p. 119). Inference: adjacent steps at most 0.36 pooled SD; separates regions, not neighbours.

measures.name: b, anterior height of body
measures.ct_mask_recipe: Cranio-caudal distance between anterior superior and anterior inferior body corners; Inference: exclude the dens at C2.
measures.level_pattern: C2 tallest, cervical minimum C5, rising to C7; lumbar rises L1 to L3, dips L4, L5 largest; L1 b significantly shorter than its d. Inference: largest steps C2/C3 -1.25, C6/C7 +1.18, L1/L2 +0.86 pooled SD.

measures.name: c, superior width of body (upper end-plate depth)
measures.ct_mask_recipe: As a, along the superior end plate; C2 placement below the dens not stated by the paper.
measures.level_pattern: Rises C2 to C7 (C4 = C5); lumbar flat 33.5-34.7. Paper: cervical base of one vertebra fits roof of the next accurately (p. 118). Inference: a(n) and c(n+1) means differ 0.1-0.5 mm cervical, 0.0-0.7 mm lumbar.

measures.name: d, posterior height of body
measures.ct_mask_recipe: Cranio-caudal distance between posterior superior and posterior inferior body corners; Inference: on a projection the posterior line is the most posterior outline, not the concave mid-sagittal wall.
measures.level_pattern: C2 tallest by far; C3-C6 flat; C7 rises; d > b at every cervical level (p. 118); lumbar about 27, L5 shortest and significantly shorter than its b (p. 119).

measures.name: k, body diagonal
measures.definition: P3 (infero-anterior) to P2 (supero-posterior), to fix the quadrangular shape
measures.page: Fig. 1, p. 116 (PDF 2); p. 117 (PDF 3); Table 1, p. 118 (PDF 4); p. 119 (PDF 5)
measures.ct_mask_recipe: Distance between antero-inferior and postero-superior corners in the sagittal frame.
measures.level_pattern: Falls C2 to C5-C6, C7 slightly up; lumbar rises L1 to L4, slight fall L5. Angle a-d about 90 deg in all lumbar vertebrae (p. 119); Inference (law of cosines on means): L1 88.0 to L5 96.8, C3 102.0, C4 101.3 deg.

measures.name: e and f, spinous tip from posterior body corners
measures.definition: e: P2 to P5; f: P4 to P5
measures.page: Fig. 1, p. 116 (PDF 2); p. 117 (PDF 3); Table 1, p. 118 (PDF 4); p. 119 (PDF 5)
measures.ct_mask_recipe: P5 = posterior-most point of the posterior elements normal to the anterior wall line in the sagittal frame; distances from P2 and P4. Inference: use the lateral silhouette so bifid cervical tips are not missed.
measures.radiograph_recipe: Lateral only; C7 tip may be hidden by clavicle, humerus and ribs.
measures.level_pattern: e > f at every level (tip below mid-body height, Inference); cervical long at C2, low at C3-C4, steep rise to C7; lumbar rise to L3, fall to L5. Inference: strongest steps f C2/C3 -2.14, e C6/C7 +1.98, f C6/C7 +1.63, f L4/L5 -0.95 pooled SD.

measures.name: alpha, spinous process inclination
measures.definition: Computed: angle at P4 between the posterior prolongation of a and f (Fig. 1 inset); Inference: positive when the tip lies caudal to the inferior end-plate line
measures.page: Fig. 1, p. 116 (PDF 2); p. 117 (PDF 3); Table 2, p. 118 (PDF 4); p. 119 (PDF 5)
measures.ct_mask_recipe: Angle in the sagittal frame between P3->P4 prolonged and P4->P5.
measures.level_pattern: Cervical peak C3, minimum C6; lumbar rises L1 to L5 (text says L1 to L3). Inference: recomputed from means matches within 1.0 deg except C2 (-2.7) and L2 (-0.2).

measures.name: L, overall vertebral length
measures.definition: Computed: distance from the anterior wall line to the parallel line through P5 (Fig. 1); Inference: a + f cos(alpha), reproducing Table 2 within 0.05 mm (0.22 at C7)
measures.ct_mask_recipe: AP extent of the whole instance from anterior body wall to spinous tip in the vertebra's frame.
measures.level_pattern: Cervical shortest C3, longest C7; lumbar longest L3, shortest L5 (p. 120). Steps C2/C3 -6.1, C5/C6 +7.3, C6/C7 +6.1, L4/L5 -5.9 mm.

measures.name: VBH and VBW, average body height and width
measures.definition: VBH average distance between superior and inferior surfaces; VBW average distance between anterior and posterior lines in lateral view; Inference: exactly (b+d)/2 and (a+c)/2
measures.ct_mask_recipe: Average of the two heights and of the two end-plate depths of the body subregion.
measures.level_pattern: C2 only level taller than deep; C3-C7 deeper than tall, widening like a pyramid; lumbar width > height, no significant change L1-L5. Inference: VBW/VBH 0.78 C2, 1.06-1.21 C3-C7, 1.24-1.29 lumbar.

level_details.detail: Covered by the skull in all films; not measured.

About 10 percent unclear (n 130/141). Tallest body (b 16.6, d 19.0), smallest c (12.6), VBW < VBH, spinous process longer than C3's (e 40.0, f 36.6, L 51.3 vs 34.4, 30.6, 45.2). Inference: C2/C3 steps -1.82 (d), -2.14 (f), -1.69 (e), -1.25 (b), +1.21 (c) pooled SD.
Nearly identical bodies; shortest vertebrae (L 45.2-48.9); alpha peak 14.4 at C3. Inference: adjacent body measures differ < 1 mm and < 0.6 pooled SD.
e, f and L jump (L 56.2); alpha lowest (3.8); one measurement missing (n 140).
About 10 percent obscured by clavicle, humerus and ribs (n 126/141); longest cervical (L 62.3, e 49.6, f 46.6); T1 not measured.
No thoracic data (rib overlap). L1 anteriorly wedged (b 25.4 < d 27.1, significant), most negative alpha (-5.8).
Almost cylindrical bodies of nearly equal size (said of all lumbar bodies); L3 longest (L 85.2) with largest e and f.
Posteriorly wedged (d 25.7 < b 28.3, significant); shortest lumbar (L 77.4); largest alpha (8.2); smallest lumbar a, d and f. Sacrum not measured.
Five large solid bones in pronounced lordosis with slightly inclined processes (impression; lordosis not measured).

errors.value: up to 10 percent cervical, < 5 percent lumbar; less than between-subject variability
about 10 percent overall; Inference: CV 7.0-16.8 percent cervical, 6.0-11.2 percent lumbar
not reported (no observer count, repeatability or test named)

pearls_pitfalls.text: Standardise films: same apparatus and film, 150 cm cervical and 100 cm lumbar, tube on C4 and L3, positioning against neck and hip rotation.
Correct magnification to the mid-sagittal plane before comparing film and anatomical sizes; the object-to-film distance is not given.
C1 is lost under the skull, thoracic vertebrae under the ribs; about 1 in 10 C2 unclear and about 1 in 10 C7 hidden by clavicle, humerus and ribs.
The model ignores articular processes, treats the spinous process as a triangle and the body as a square box.
Keep level-specific values; the dimensions change progressively from level to level.
'Lumbar is two or more times cervical' holds only for end-plate depths a and c; not for heights, k, e, f or L (Inference from Tables 1-2).
'Width' is antero-posterior depth on the lateral view, not transverse width.
Inference: with one central ray on C4 or L3, end plates of C2, C7, L1 and L5 are struck obliquely (double contours); rotation doubles the posterior wall; not discussed by the paper.
Inference: lumbar films were side-lying and cervical films standing; intra-vertebral measures are affected only through projection.

instructions.text: On a lateral cervical film expect C1 to be unmeasurable under the skull base; anchor the count on C2, confirmed by a body taller than deep (VBH 17.8 vs VBW 13.95) and a long posterior element (L 51.3 vs 45.2 at C3).
Mark P1-P5 on every vertebra in lateral view: four body corners and the spinous tip where a line parallel to the anterior wall touches it.

Measure a, b, c, d, k, e, f; compute L = a + f cos(alpha), alpha the angle of P4-P5 from the posteriorly prolonged inferior end-plate line, positive caudal (Inference, checked against Table 2 and Fig. 1); divide distances by magnification first.

Inference: from a CT instance mask take points from the instance's lateral silhouette in its own sagittal frame, take the spinous tip from the silhouette (bifid cervical tips), and leave the dens out of C2 body heights.
Find the lower cervical spine by the posterior element: L, e and f step up sharply C5 to C6 to C7 (L 48.9, 56.2, 62.3; e 35.4, 41.5, 49.6).
Inference: do not separate C3, C4 and C5 by body measures (adjacent means differ < 1 mm against SDs 1.2-1.9 mm); count from C2.
Expect C7 hidden in about 1 film in 10; Inference: if the last visible cervical vertebra's L is nearer 56.2 (C6) than 62.3 (C7), suspect C6, weighing e and f too since L has no SD.

Within a known lumbar run, b/d < 1 marks L1 (0.94), b/d > 1 marks L5 (1.10), L2-L4 near 1.00; guard: all cervical levels have b < d and no T12 data exist, so an anterior wedge alone does not prove L1 (Inference).
Read alpha: negative at L1-L2, near zero L3, largest at L5 (8.2 deg); Inference: no SD, so its separating power is unknown, and L2's value disagrees with the other columns.
Expect L3 longest and L5 shortest lumbar vertebra; Inference: a vertebra about 6 mm shorter in L than its upper neighbour with a posterior wedge is the L5 candidate.

Inference: a of one vertebra matches c of the next within 0.7 mm at the means; use it to confirm two instances face each other across a disc, not to detect a skipped level, since a and c change slowly.
Treat radiographic differences under about 1.5 mm as possible method error (0.5 mm calipers + 1.0 mm parallax); SDs are about 10 percent of the mean.
Do not take anomaly priors, female or older-age values from this paper (men 20-38, abnormal spines excluded).
No thoracic data; do not extrapolate to T1-T12.

bordercall: (a) Anomaly priors: none; the paper assumed, and did not test, seven cervical and five lumbar vertebrae, and excluded abnormal spines (p. 115, PDF 1; p. 117, PDF 3).

(b) a, c, b, d are radiographic counterparts of Panjabi's lower and upper end-plate depths and anterior and posterior body heights for C2-C7 and L1-L5 (Table 1, p. 118, PDF 4); Inference: they are silhouette corner-to-corner distances including rim and lipping, magnification-corrected by an assumed geometry, so compare numerically with the Panjabi priors before pooling.

(b) Candidate additions: k, e, f, alpha and L; Inference: they separate C2/C3, C5-C7 and L4/L5 better than the body measures. They start from the body corners, so they are not a lamina-based spinous process length.

(b) Table 1 gives per-level mean and SD for seven measures (univariate emissions for radiograph features); no covariances (in the 1982 report only); Table 2 has no SDs. No canal, pedicle, facet or transverse measures.
(b) Inference: from a mask use the left-right projected silhouette; the mid-sagittal slice shortens e, f and L where the tip is bifid or off midline.

(c) Method error < +/-0.5 mm plus <= +/-1.0 mm parallax (up to 10 percent cervical, < 5 percent lumbar); Table 1 SDs (about 10 percent) are biology plus error (p. 119, PDF 5). Inference: add sigma about 1 mm for radiograph-derived features, none for CT.
(d) Covariates: men only, 20-38 years (mean 26.8), mean stature 174.7 cm, likely Israeli (Inference); no dependence on sex, age or size reported here (in the 1982 report) (p. 115, PDF 1).
gaps: Text implies cervical e and f are lowest at C3 (p. 119, PDF 5); Table 1 puts the minimum at C4 (e 33.6 vs 34.4, f 30.4 vs 30.6), within SD.
Text says alpha increased from L1 to L3 (p. 119, PDF 5, subscript checked at 600 dpi); Table 2 shows it rising through L5.
The lumbar paragraph cites 'a to k; Table 2' (p. 119, PDF 5); a to k are in Table 1.

'All dimensions' lumbar two or more times cervical (p. 119, PDF 5) holds only for a and c (2.04-2.75); not b (1.53-2.23), d (1.35-2.02), k (1.73-2.01), e (1.04-1.69), f (0.94-1.66) or L (1.24-1.88) (Inference from Tables 1-2).
e > f is read as downward inclination (p. 119, PDF 5) though alpha is negative at L1-L3; 'downward' means below mid-body height (Inference).
'L3 has the longest spinous process in the human body' (p. 119, PDF 5) is unsupported: no thoracic data, and e, f, L run from the body.
Denominators: 141 cervical and 157 lumbar spines (p. 115) vs 157 men (p. 120); missing L1 (3), L5 (1), C6 (1) unexplained.
Alpha recomputed from table means fails at C2 and L2 (Inference); no SD for alpha, L, VBH, VBW.

Unstated: object-to-film distance and magnification factor, how levels were counted, C2 corner placement below the dens, observers and repeatability, the significance test, covariances between measures.
No women, no subjects over 38, no anomaly counts, no thoracic or sacral values, no disc heights or spacing, no alignment angles, no canal, pedicle or facet measures.
Inference from memory: references misspell Stagnara as 'Stagmara' (p. 120, PDF 6) and Andriacchi as 'Andriaechi' (p. 115, PDF 1).

Inference from memory: Panjabi's dry-bone series give the same body depths and heights plus canal, pedicle and facet measures; Hinck 1966 measures the canal on lateral and AP films; compare a-d numerically with the generator's Panjabi priors.
